diagnostics.evidence:
STATIC: R3v2Pool._hard_reset() (runner lines 173-190) restores v, u, the 10 _CONDUCT conductance arrays, cp_firing_states, cp_last_spike_time, cp_eligibility_trace, cp_external_input_current, and dopamine concentration/_rule_state -- but never touches cp_refractory_timers, cp_prev_firing_states, cp_neuron_activity_ema, or cp_neuron_firing_thresholds. This is not unique to this file: it is byte-for-byte the same primitive/omission as R2Pool._hard_reset (_onebrain_integration_r2_threefactor_selforganized.py:251-267), which R3v2's _f1-_f4 are imported from verbatim. enable_homeostasis=False in every merged organ config (D6_CONFIG, COMPREHENSION_CONFIG, r3_extra) makes cp_neuron_activity_ema/cp_neuron_firing_thresholds provably inert for this runner (bridge.py's _homeostasis_active gate never fires) -- but cp_refractory_timers/cp_prev_firing_states are core Izhikevich-step bookkeeping, updated unconditionally every step (bridge.py:8193,8225,8445) regardless of config, so 2 of the 4 named arrays are a live leak vector here.

DYNAMIC A (strict control -- mechanism physically zeroed via mode='da_lesioned', .train() never called): direct array inspection confirms real leakage -- cp_refractory_timers/cp_prev_firing_states go from all-zero (fresh pool) to 31/1752 then 33/1752 nonzero after successive amb_read()-style reads, overlapping 5/24 sel_agent neurons + 1/24 sel_patient neurons. But calling the PRODUCTION amb_read(p_agent, ambig, band=True) 3x identically on this pool gave BITWISE-IDENTICAL margins all three times (0.0005555555555555314, x3) -- with the DA/reward pathway physically severed, this leaked residue does not propagate into the measured output on this topology.

DYNAMIC B (the condition _f2 actually exercises -- mode='intact', mechanism live, still .train() NEVER called): the SAME production amb_read(p_agent, ambig, band=True) called 3x identically gave THREE DIFFERENT margins: 0.0016666666666666496, 0.0037962962962962976, 0.000740740740740727 -- confirmed non-reproducible. Root-caused directly by instrumenting cross_weights() across repeated reads with zero training: w0->A (the candidate edge) climbed 0.05 (build value) -> 0.4593 -> 0.868 -> 1.2663 -> 1.6537 -> 2.0302 over 5 successive amb_read() calls with no .train() anywhere. Cause: enable_stdp/enable_reward_modulation are GLOBAL always-on config flags (not scoped to .train() episodes) and the 'wm_to_sel_r2' plasticity gate opens once in __init__ and never closes, so a 'read' step and a 'train' step are mechanically identical; R3v2 inherits R2's _f1-_f4/amb_read verbatim, which assume reads are reward-free (true in R2, whose _drive(reward=0.0) explicitly zeroes current_reward_signal every call) but R3v2's DA-population credit pathway is never gated by any drive-call argument, so that assumption is silently broken.

CONTROL: the same repeated-read test holding BASE_POOL (the structurally-never-a-candidate 'none' control) is leak-immune in BOTH modes -- bitwise identical every time (0.0011111111111111183). The leak concentrates exactly in the p_agent/p_patient (candidate-pool) reads that ARE the numerator of _f2's delta_agent/delta_patient -- never in the control it's compared against.

ORDER: none-then-agent vs agent-then-none on fresh same-seed pools gave identical deltas when each condition is read only once (mode=da_lesioned) -- the dominant, unambiguously order/history-dependent confound is same-condition repetition, i.e. exactly what amb_read's own internal N_READS=3 loop does, and what _f2's two-battery (intact-then-lesion) structure does.

SCALE: the confirmed confound's magnitude in the untrained probe (0.0007-0.0038 read-to-read swing; weight movable >0.4/read from W0=0.05) is comparable to or larger than the entire signal the banked NO-GO turns on -- delta_agent_intact ranges only 0.0027-0.0060 across all 6 real seeds, all under F2_INTACT_FLOOR=0.008, missing by as little as 0.00198 on the best seed. The REAL post-training candidate weight (F3.grown_correct_mean, seeds 42-44) averages only ~0.23-0.24 -- i.e. the true operating point sits deep inside the same low-weight range (0.05-2+) where the probe showed reads alone move weight by an order of magnitude and swing margin NON-monotonically (margin rose then collapsed toward 0 as weight kept climbing in the probe, a likely firing-rate ceiling effect) -- so the confound's magnitude at the true operating point is plausible but its SIGN could not be pinned without instrumenting a fully-trained pool (out of reasonable scope for a read-only audit: would require duplicating a full 400-episode .train() run). Also consistent with the classic C2 signature: delta_agent_lesion is not exactly 0 on any seed (9.3e-05 to 1.48e-3), plausibly the same always-on STDP nudging the nominally-zeroed candidate weights away from 0 during the lesion battery's own reads.

Given F2 is the SOLE blocker (every other arm 6/6) and the confirmed confound's magnitude matches or exceeds the floor-shortfall, this is the highest-value pattern the audit is looking for: a razor-thin NO-GO that a confirmed, reproducible read-isolation leak plausibly suppressed.

R4Pool._hard_reset() (runner lines 240-252) restores only cp_membrane_potential_v, cp_recovery_variable_u, the 10 _CONDUCT conductance arrays, cp_firing_states, cp_hebb_coactivity_trace, cp_external_input_current -- it NEVER touches cp_refractory_timers, cp_prev_firing_states, cp_neuron_activity_ema, or cp_neuron_firing_thresholds (the exact 4 arrays the C2 fix added). Confirmed structurally IDENTICAL in shape to the pre-fix _crossedge_surprise_metacog_derisk.py _hard_reset (same _CONDUCT tuple, same firing_states/hebb_coactivity_trace lines, nothing else).

EMPIRICAL (seed 42, cross-edge weight forced to exactly 0.0 via the F2 lesion step, R4Pool freshly built with NO r4.train() ever called): a 100-step no-hold drive changes cp_refractory_timers and cp_prev_firing_states (max abs diff = 1.0 vs pre-drive) and hard_reset() called again afterward does NOT restore them to the original baseline (max abs diff still 1.0) -- direct proof these 2 of the 4 critical arrays leak. cp_neuron_activity_ema/cp_neuron_firing_thresholds were present (thresholds array had 1042 nonzero entries) but did not move in this particular 100-step window, so they were not the source of THIS leak, though they remain structurally unrestored.

Two IDENTICAL no-hold reads called back-to-back (same _hard_reset()+_drive() primitives the runner itself uses, mechanism zeroed, no training) were NOT bitwise identical: read1={'gen': 0.080625,'perc': 0.0959375}, read2={'gen': 0.08,'perc': 0.09625}.

ORDER-DEPENDENCE, isolated fresh-pool test (mechanism zeroed, no training): reversing which condition (no-hold vs hold) is read first flips the measured delta's SIGN exactly -- seed 42: forward(no-hold-then-hold) delta=+0.00125, reversed(hold-then-no-hold) delta=-0.00125; seed 43: forward delta=-0.0009375, reversed delta=+0.0009375. Exact sign inversion is the same signature reported in the banked C2 fix finding's own low/high order-reversal table.

REALISTIC in-context test (full runner path: R4Pool -> train() -> _f1() -> _f4() -> _f2(), the runner's own actual order): forward (real) order reproduced the banked finding's exact numbers almost exactly -- seed 42 delta_intact=0.01323 (finding: 0.0132), delta_lesion=-0.00010 (finding: -0.0001); seed 100 delta_intact=0.01104 (finding: 0.0110), delta_lesion=-0.00031 (finding: -0.0003) -- confirming the probe faithfully reproduces the original harness. Reversing the F2 read order (held-then-base instead of base-then-held) on a freshly rebuilt+retrained pool at the SAME seed shifted delta_intact by -0.00198 (seed 42: 0.01323->0.01125) and -0.00010 (seed 100: 0.01104->0.01094), and delta_lesion by +0.00063 (seed 42: -0.00010->+0.00052) and -0.00010 (seed 100: -0.00031->-0.00042). Despite these shifts, F2 PASS remained TRUE under BOTH read orders on BOTH seeds tested: delta_intact stayed above F2_INTACT_FLOOR=0.010 in every case (worst case 0.01094, seed 100 reversed) and |delta_lesion| stayed far below F2_LESION_RATIO(0.34)*|delta_intact| in every case (worst case 0.00052 vs a 0.00383-0.00450 threshold).

Seed 100 was deliberately chosen as the tightest-margin seed in the bank (delta_intact=0.0110, closest to the 0.010 floor) and survived order reversal with only a 0.0001 shift -- the leak's real-world magnitude in this specific, already-trained/already-read-many-times execution context is much smaller than in the naive isolated fresh-pool probe. Only seeds 42 and 100 were dynamically re-verified (not all 6); seeds 43/44/101/102 were not independently re-tested for order-reversal, so a full 6-seed reverification is still the honest next step, not a completed clearance.

diagnostics.evidence: STATIC: `EncodeGatePool._hard_reset()` (runner lines 240-252) restores cp_membrane_potential_v, cp_recovery_variable_u, the 10 cp_conductance_g_* arrays (_CONDUCT), cp_firing_states, cp_hebb_coactivity_trace, cp_external_input_current — it does NOT touch cp_refractory_timers, cp_prev_firing_states, cp_neuron_activity_ema, or cp_neuron_firing_thresholds. This is byte-for-byte the same omission the C2 finding fixed. Confirmed the bug is genuinely present, not merely stylistic: after training the edge for real (grown w=0.7121, seed 42) and taking one intact 'high' (CONTRADICT) read that made encode_gate actually fire (2/48 neurons went refractory, activity_ema drifted 9.2039->9.5698, firing_thresholds drifted -2013.5376->-2013.3293), calling _hard_reset() left all 4 arrays exactly at those post-fire values (verified by direct array snapshot) -- the reset genuinely fails to isolate a 'hot' state from the next read. Repeating read_gate('high') 3x on that same hot pool gave NON-bitwise-identical outputs: 0.07972222222222221, 0.07996527777777777, 0.07986111111111109 (~0.3% relative noise) -- a real, dynamically-confirmed leak in the INTACT/trained condition. HOWEVER: the task's decisive test (mechanism/cross-edge ZEROED + NO training, read twice) is CLEAN here -- bitwise identical across two full read_gate('high') calls (0.0/0.013055555555555565 both times), across 6 raw sub-reads (all exactly 0.0), and across reversed condition order (low->high vs high->low, both orders give identical 'high'=0.0/0.013055... and 'low'=0.0/0.0).
